problem:
Consider the following matrices:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-5 & 2 \\ -12 & 5\end{aligned}],\,D=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}],\,P=[\begin{aligned}-1 & a \\ -2 & b\end{aligned}]
$$

Given that $D={P}^{-1}AP,$ find the value of $\frac{b}{a}.$
worked_solution:
From the diagonal matrix $D=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]$, we deduce that the eigenvalues of $A$ are ${\lambda }_{1}=-1$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=1.$

So, the second column of $P$ corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{2}=1.$ 

Now, we simply need to find an eigenvector that corresponds to ${\lambda }_{2}=1.$ Computing $A-I,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}A-I & =[\begin{aligned}-5 & 2 \\ -12 & 5\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-6 & 2 \\ -12 & 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to its row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-6 & 2 & 0 \\ -12 & 4 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-6 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=\frac{1}{3}{x}_{2}.$  Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, setting ${x}_{2}=3,$ we get the eigenvector 

$$
{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, $\frac{b}{a}=\frac{3}{1}=3.$
